stories.title: Within-country income inequality alters the quantity and composition of projected global food demand
stories.description: Income and income distribution have key roles in shaping food demand. However, current global food and land-use models rely on average national income to project food demand, ignoring within-country income distributions. This study embeds estimates of future intranational inequality into a global food system model to quantify the combined effects of income distribution, socioeconomic development and climate change on global food systems. Here, using scenario modelling, we find that food demand projections that consider national income distributions differ substantially from equivalent projections based on average income, particularly for high-value commodities such as animal-source foods. In a scenario with high intranational inequality (Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 3, ‘regional rivalry’), disaggregating income groups decreased projected animal calorie demand in 2100 by 10.4%, while total calorie demand decreased by 3.29%. Future inequality within countries is likely to impact the quantity and composition of global food demand and should therefore be represented in long-term models of the food system. While income distribution is a key determinant of food demand, it is not fully captured in current global food and land-use models. By embedding estimates of future intranational inequality into scenario analysis, this study quantifies the combined effects of income distribution, socioeconomic development and climate change on global food systems.

stories.title: Solar integrated biomass to dimethyl ether synthesis via auto thermal reforming and water electrolysis for efficient CO2 utilization
stories.description: The shift toward low-carbon fuels increasingly depends on processes that can utilize biogenic resources, incorporate external CO2, and operate reliably with renewable electricity. This work introduces an integrated biomass-to-dimethyl ether (DME) pathway that links autothermal reforming of rice husk with a solid oxide electrolysis unit and a solar photovoltaic field. The aim is to quantify how solar-assisted, grid-buffered electrification of this route affects energy efficiency, plant-level CO2 utilization, and production cost relative to a grid-powered benchmark. An expanded multi-parameter decision space was constructed to capture interactions among ATR (auto-thermal reforming) conversion, operating temperature, solar irradiance, hydrogen generation, and catalyst behavior. The system was optimized using the recent R-DNEA (reference-point-based evolutionary algorithm) multi-objective algorithm to simultaneously raise overall energy efficiency, lower the net carbon balance (NCB), and reduce the levelized cost of DME (LC-DME). The solar-assisted configuration increased plant-level CO2 utilization from 0.651 to 0.989 kg/s, improved carbon efficiency from 85.47% to 86.48%, and shifted the gate-to-gate net carbon balance from − 0.320 to − 0.752 kg/s when electricity-related emissions are excluded; when grid-import emissions are included, net fixation is retained only for grid emission factors below 12.9 g CO2/kWh (grid-powered) and 41.3 g CO2/kWh (solar-assisted). The integrated design produced 4.52 kg/s of DME while strengthening thermal coupling between the ATR and electrolysis units through the beneficial use of electrolyser-derived oxygen. An annual electricity balance shows that a load-matched PV array (89.4 MWAC) with a short-duration battery buffer supplies 26.7% of the 679.3 GWh/yr electricity demand, while the grid supplies the remaining 73.3%. On this basis, the LC-DME is 385.1 USD/ton for the grid-powered configuration and 478.8 USD/ton for the solar-assisted configuration, and the solar-assisted route becomes cost-competitive only when the grid tariff exceeds about 99.6 USD/MWh, which equals the levelized cost of the PV-delivered electricity. Multi-objective optimization raised the overall energy efficiency to 86.12% at an NCB of − 0.713 kg/s, with a re-based LC-DME of about 465.7 USD/ton. These results show that coupling renewable electrolysis with controlled ATR chemistry achieves net CO2 fixation within the plant boundary, whereas the economic benefit of solar assistance depends mainly on the grid tariff and the PV capital cost. The framework also provides practical guidance for renewable-fuel plant design.

stories.title: Effects of high dietary inclusion of black soldier fly larvae meal on the serum metabolome of healthy adult dogs
stories.description: The escalating global demand for animal protein has increased interest in sustainable alternatives for pet nutrition, with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFL) emerging as a promising nutrient-rich ingredient. As unconventional ingredients are increasingly used in pet food, understanding their systemic metabolic effects is important. This study investigated the effects of including partially defatted BSFL meal at levels corresponding to 0%, 50%, and 100% replacement of poultry viscera meal on the serum metabolome of six healthy adult dogs (mean age 5.3 ± 1.03 years; mean body weight 23.0 ± 2.7 kg) over 22-day experimental periods, using a double Latin square design. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using one-dimensional ¹H nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, followed by principal component analysis (PCA) and pathway analysis. A total of 40 serum metabolites were identified, and individual metabolite concentrations did not differ among dietary treatments (P > 0.05 for all metabolites). PCA also showed substantial overlap among treatments, with no clear separation between dietary groups. Pathway analysis identified glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism; glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism; alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism; and phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthesis as pathways meeting the statistical criteria applied in the analysis. However, these pathway-analysis results should be interpreted cautiously because none of the individual metabolite concentrations differed among dietary treatments. Overall, high dietary inclusion of partially defatted BSFL meal did not induce detectable alterations in the serum metabolomic profile of healthy adult dogs under the short-term conditions evaluated. These findings suggest short-term serum metabolomic stability following BSFL inclusion, although larger and longer-term studies are warranted to confirm these results and further evaluate its use as an alternative protein ingredient in dog nutrition.

stories.title: Insights into collapsibility and structural behaviors of unsaturated loess from a novel discrete element model
stories.description: The existing microscopic contact model based on capillary force can effectively simulate the consolidation and collapsibility behaviors of unsaturated loess under low saturation (≤ 30%), yet it fails to characterize the mechanical responses of loess under high saturation conditions and neglects inter-particle chemical bonding. Therefore, an improved microscopic contact model is proposed considering capillary force for full-range saturation conditions, and chemical bonding force by the secondary development and discrete element method (DEM). After the reliability and accuracy are verified through two-particle single-contact model tests, numerical collapse tests are carried out to explore the multi-factor influences of initial water content, relative compaction and chemical bonding strength on the collapsibility deformation of loess. The results demonstrate that the improved model expands the applicable saturation range and can accurately reproduce the wetting-induced collapsibility characteristics of structured loess. The increase of water content accelerates the attenuation of inter-particle capillary force and the softening of chemical bonding strength, which significantly enhances the collapsibility of loess. Higher relative compaction and stronger chemical bonding can effectively inhibit the collapse deformation of loess. Microscopic mechanism analysis reveals that loess collapse is essentially the structural stability loss caused by the weakening of inter-particle connection under hydro-mechanical-chemical coupling effects. These findings can provide a theoretical basis for macro-micro mechanism analysis of unsaturated loess and the prevention of loess collapsibility hazards in geotechnical engineering.

stories.title: Wulcea Redefines Everyday Winter Wear with Graphene Warmth, Certified Safety, and Lasting Care
stories.description: As heated apparel shifts from niche outdoor gear into everyday commuter wardrobes, modern shoppers expect refined garment craftsmanship backed by attentive service. Since its founding, Wulcea has built its entire heated apparel collection around a clear principle: enduring product quality and responsive customer care belong together, giving buyers confidence before purchase and peace of mind long after.
